findings: I verified the frozen JAR ZIP against its checksum, read its Stata data dictionary and author data-description and coding supplements, and inspected the original published Table 6 on printed pages 523–524. The deposit has 293,815 firm-year observations and 18 fields. It supplies the authors’ adoption classifications and does not supply baseline outcomes, the continuous reporting controls or executable programs.

Table 6 contains nine regressions. In incentives, behavior and environment order, the printed sample sizes are 65,752, 58,739 and 67,390 for price impact, 46,055, 41,272 and 47,277 for quoted spread, and 24,253, 22,914 and 24,984 for implied cost of equity. The nine distinct target records and the status CSV agree on each published sample size. The estimands concern serious versus label adoption, with firm-clustered inference and industry, country and year fixed effects.

I reviewed the executed SAS source and native log. Of 255,229 author-deposit firm-years in 1990–2005, direct Worldscope annual ISIN/year joins produce 204,065 matches including 25,147 ambiguous firm-years. The Datastream-to-Worldscope route gives 192,837 observations with exactly one code and fiscal end within the recorded price coverage window. These are input-coverage counts. The available annual fundamentals and dated matching diagnostics cannot count as an estimated paper regression.

Daske et al. (2008), Table 1 note on p. 1102, identifies New Markets venues and explicitly defines original Worldscope index membership as time-invariant. Present-day Worldscope field 05661 exists. Original-vintage agreement and historical U.S. listing and New Markets assignments by firm were not verified. The continuous reporting-level controls, including adopters’ pre-adoption means, and the final sample screens were not constructed.

Hail and Leuz (2006), Appendix A.1–A.2 on pp. 525–528, supplies the four implied-cost-of-capital methods. The forecast, pricing, payout, inflation and related sample inputs have not been assembled and tested for these firms. This is an unresolved construction requirement rather than evidence of unavailable formulas or a missing subscription.

All nine primary Table 6 regressions remain unexecuted. No Stata estimates, sample comparisons against realized regression samples, or numerical replication rates exist for this paper. The native SAS preflight completed in 21.88 seconds. Table 3 and alternative reduced specifications do not replace missing Table 6 evidence. I accept the documented, bounded attempt and its aggregate diagnostics.
